images.title: Always, sometimes or never
images.purpose: Shows the core move of the practice: sorting a statement as always, sometimes or never true, with one short reason for each.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Three equal columns side by side, each headed by one word with one card under it.
images.exact_structure: Three equal rounded columns. Left column headed always with a green (#009E73) header bar; its card reads 6a + 9b = 3(2a + 3b). Middle column headed sometimes with an amber (#E69F00) header bar; its card reads 6 + 3 = 9, 6 + 6 = 12. Right column headed never with a vermilion (#D55E00) header bar; its card reads 12b − 28. Exactly 3 columns and 3 cards. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A statement is always true with an algebra reason, sometimes true with one example and one non-example, never true when it can never work.
images.description: Shows the core move of the practice: sorting a statement as always, sometimes or never true, with one short reason for each.
images.context: Always: multiple of 6 plus multiple of 9 is a multiple of 3. Sometimes: multiple of 6 plus multiple of 3 is a multiple of 9 (9 yes, 12 no). Never: 8(7b − 3) − 4(11b + 1) = 12b − 28 = 12(b − 2) − 4, never a multiple of 12.

image_decisions.why: Three verdict columns show the sorting this practice asks for.
